hypothesis: With the ground truth that steers the oracle held apart from the ground truth it is scored on, how much of H2's error would a perfect matching stage remove?
training: none -- trained H2 checkpoints, inference and substitution only
method: gt>0 pixels split 50/50 (seed 0); initial <- clamp(initial + 1.0*a*(gt-final), 0, 11) on the FIT half only, 16 iterations; EPE/D1 pooled separately on both halves; the verdict reads the EVAL half
known_limitation: refinement is convolutional, so a corrected FIT pixel propagates to its EVAL neighbours; the EVAL number remains an upper bound on what a realizable matching stage buys, and says nothing about a refinement stage retrained against such an input.
